package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to patched Google Camera/Samsung Camera apps (pre-July 2019)
package_info.why_malicious: The package exploits a vulnerability in Android camera app intent handling (CVE-2019-2234) to bypass camera and microphone permissions, enabling covert photo, video, and audio capture, as well as exfiltration of sensitive data (including GPS metadata) to a remote C&C server. It maintains persistent C&C communication for remote exploitation, operating without user consent or awareness.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app main activity / background service

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a C&C command, the code sends a crafted intent to the camera app to take a photo, stores the resulting image in accessible storage, and uploads the image file to a remote C&C server, enabling covert photo capture and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app programmatically triggers the camera to take photos without user interaction or holding the camera permission, exploiting a vulnerability to bypass Android's security model.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit user consent and the CAMERA permission to access the camera; this app bypasses those controls and initiates photo capture from the background.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate camera or automation apps may use camera intents, but only with user consent, visible UI, and proper permissions.
key_indicators: Background app sending camera capture intent without CAMERA permission
No user interaction required for photo capture
Captured images automatically uploaded to remote server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C&C command or proximity sensor event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a C&C command or proximity sensor event, the code sends a crafted intent to the camera app to record video (including audio), saves the video file to accessible storage, and uploads the video to a remote C&C server, enabling covert video/audio capture and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app records video and audio without user knowledge or the CAMERA/MICROPHONE permissions, exploiting the intent vulnerability to bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit user consent and CAMERA/MICROPHONE permissions for video/audio recording; this app circumvents those requirements and operates covertly.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate automation or security apps may record video, but only with user awareness, visible UI, and explicit permissions.
key_indicators: Video/audio recording triggered by background app without CAMERA/MICROPHONE permissions
No user interaction or visible UI during recording
Automatic upload of video files to remote server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after capturing a photo or video, the code parses EXIF metadata from the media file to extract GPS coordinates, then uploads the location data to a remote C&C server, enabling covert exfiltration of sensitive location information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app extracts and exfiltrates GPS location data embedded in media files without user consent, enabling tracking of the device's physical location.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not access or transmit location metadata from photos or videos without explicit user permission and clear disclosure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Photo management apps may read EXIF data for sorting or mapping, but do not covertly transmit location data to external servers.
key_indicators: Automated EXIF parsing for GPS data in background
Network transmission of extracted location data
No user interaction or notification during data access

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C&C command or proximity sensor event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors the proximity sensor to detect when a voice call is in progress (e.g., phone held to ear), then triggers video and audio recording to capture both sides of the conversation, saving the recording to storage and uploading it to a remote C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app covertly records private conversations by using the proximity sensor to detect calls and trigger recording, all without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not record calls or use sensors to trigger covert recording without explicit user approval and legal compliance.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Call recording apps exist, but require explicit user permission, visible UI, and compliance with legal requirements.
key_indicators: Proximity sensor used to trigger covert recording
Audio/video capture during voice calls without user interaction
Automatic exfiltration of call recordings to remote server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At app startup and during background operation, the code establishes and maintains a persistent connection to a remote C&C server, continuously waiting for and executing remote commands such as photo, video, and audio capture.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app maintains a stealthy, persistent connection to an external server, enabling remote attackers to control device sensors and exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not maintain persistent C&C connections for remote exploitation or allow remote control of device sensors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate apps use persistent connections for notifications or messaging, but not for remote device control or covert data capture.
key_indicators: Persistent background network connection to external server
Remote command execution for sensor access
No user-facing functionality justifying persistent connectivity

attack_chain.action: Malicious app is installed and establishes a persistent connection to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker can issue commands to the device.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues command to take a photo, record video, or record audio (including during calls), triggering covert media capture.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device captures sensitive media (photos, videos, audio) without user knowledge.

attack_chain.action: Captured photos and videos are stored in accessible storage; app parses EXIF data for GPS location.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive media and location data are prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: App uploads captured media and extracted GPS/location data to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to private photos, videos, audio, and location data from the device.

behavioral_signatures: Background apps sending camera or video capture intents without holding CAMERA or MICROPHONE permissions
Apps accessing and parsing EXIF GPS metadata from photos or videos without user interaction
Persistent outbound connections to unknown servers from apps not expected to require continuous network access
Media capture events triggered by proximity sensor activity in background services
file_indicators: Unexpected photos or videos appearing in device camera roll or media storage
App accessing camera or media storage without user-initiated action or visible UI
Frequent or automated access to EXIF data in app logs or storage access patterns
network_indicators: Outbound connections to C&C infrastructure (unknown IPs/domains) from non-network-centric apps
Uploads of media files (photos, videos, audio) to remote servers without user action
Persistent TCP connections initiated by background services with no user-facing justification
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that trigger camera or video capture intents without holding CAMERA or MICROPHONE permissions, especially if they only request storage permission. Flag apps that access EXIF GPS metadata or upload media files to external servers without user interaction. Use network monitoring to detect persistent outbound connections from apps not expected to maintain such connections. Alert on media capture events triggered by background services or proximity sensor events, and correlate with lack of user interaction or visible UI.
